source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Enter BMC Web UI ->  Click tab "Settings" -> Click tab "SSL Settings" -> Click " Upload CERTIFICATE MANAGEMENT" .
SSL Certificate key will be changed.
View ssl certificate match your modified settings.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Result should be human readable.
Login BMC web successfully.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: curl + jq, openssl (user-supplied cert for upload)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Upload CERTIFICATE MANAGEMENT: uploads a user-supplied certificate (POST multipart to the BMC cert endpoint); it is a security-sensitive state change + (for upload) needs the cert file. Agent can help with the generate/upload request once the user supplies the CSR settings/cert, then verify: curl -s -k -u "$BMC_USER:$BMC_PASS" https://$BMC_IP/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/NetworkProtocol/HTTPS/Certificates 2>&1 | jq .
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL Redfish certificate-list JSON after the generate/upload so the user confirms the new certificate is present/active.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: generating/uploading a certificate changes the BMC HTTPS trust/identity and can disrupt management connections; do only with user-provided values and verify connectivity after.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL recognizes an upload as a security-sensitive write and requests supplied certificate material, but guesses a multipart/API path, uses `curl -k`, combines Generate and Upload evidence and only lists certificate metadata. It does not establish accepted input format, private-key pairing, chain order, slot, activation, actual served identity or WebUI login.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires protected local certificate/key/chain validation, exact vendor upload and activation semantics, one approved change, bounded reconnect, served-chain verification and independent recovery.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 925/2291 repeats the truncated DeepSeek command and generic read/write gate without resolving formats, key possession, target slot, activation, trust validation, WebUI coverage or rollback.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: The preceding Generate row creates BMC-held key/certificate or CSR material; this Upload row instead consumes owner-supplied certificate material and must prove the uploaded identity becomes the intended served state.
historical_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No sequence-1087, Wistron-BMC-00216-V002 or cb813ffe054a3a2f draft exists in the invalidated run.
historical_reviews.v3: No V3 overlay exists for this exact case.
historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves the distinct Upload action and stated key change; ED-34 treats format, key, chain, slot and activation as Project inputs; ED-35 rejects metadata-only or insecure trust proof; ED-38 requires approval, recovery, one attempt and no automatic retry.

original_test_intent: Verify the BMC WebUI Upload Certificate Management function accepts the Project-approved certificate material, changes the intended HTTPS certificate/key state, presents readable matching settings and preserves successful BMC WebUI login.
original_method: Baseline the active certificate/chain/fingerprint, key/slot relationship and recovery access; validate the supplied certificate, chain and any private-key container locally; identify the exact vendor-supported WebUI format and activation behavior; upload once after confirmation; capture the UI/audit/state transition; monitor bounded HTTPS recovery; verify the certificate actually served by the BMC and complete a fresh trusted WebUI login.
manual_activity: An engineer supplies and approves the certificate/chain and protected key-handling model, target slot, activation and recovery. A human performs and visually checks the source WebUI upload and fresh login. Automation may prevalidate public certificate material and corroborate served state, but cannot disclose a private key, substitute the prior Generate action or issue the verdict.
required_inputs: BMC/firmware/WebUI identity and vendor Certificate Management upload specification
Approved management hostname/IP, certificate, full chain and trust anchors
Protected private key/container and passphrase handling, or documented binding to an existing BMC-generated key
Accepted file/container format, chain order, multipart fields, size and cryptographic policy
Current active certificate/chain/fingerprint/key identity/slot and trusted client baseline
Independent recovery and prior-certificate restoration method
WebUI field readability, served chain/trust and fresh-login acceptance
safety_requirements: Do not clear BMC/security/audit logs or place private keys, passwords, passphrases, tokens or complete secret-bearing upload payloads in commands, JSON or evidence.
Verify exact BMC, hostname, key pairing or existing-key binding, full chain, validity and target slot before presenting the WebUI action.
Preserve redacted pre-change public metadata and independent recovery; do not overwrite the only recoverable certificate/key state without a vendor-supported restoration path.
Obtain point-of-action approval for one upload and any separate activation/restart. Do not retry, delete certificates or change another slot on timeout.
Do not use `curl -k`, upload acceptance or a certificate-resource list as trust proof. Validate the actually served full chain, SAN/hostname and explicit trust outcome.

Stop on key mismatch, malformed/incomplete chain, wrong identity/slot, failed activation, reconnect timeout or lost access; use independent recovery and approved rollback without another blind upload.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target, upload format, protected key model, supplied public material, baseline, target slot, activation/reconnect behavior, recovery and visual/login evidence; present the exact WebUI upload action for confirmation.
After the human uploads once, capture the source UI and audit response plus redacted pending/active public metadata without exposing file contents that contain private keys.
Monitor bounded HTTPS/BMC recovery, collect complete served certificate and management state, and perform the approved fresh WebUI login/trust check.
Archive redacted evidence and stop without Generate substitution, guessed Redfish action, insecure verification, automatic upload/retry, deletion or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve the certificate/chain/key source, format, crypto policy, target slot and activation semantics.
Approve the one-time WebUI upload, service/session impact, recovery/rollback and trust/login acceptance.
Review prevalidation, UI/audit, active/served chain and access evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It identifies upload risk but does not provide or discover a supported upload action. The guessed generic Redfish list path and `-k` only read metadata and cannot prove the supplied certificate/key was accepted, activated, served or trusted; its Generate/Upload wording blurs adjacent coverage.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the exact vendor WebUI Upload control with the approved protected file/container and target slot once. Use protected discovered API and verified TLS tooling only for redacted public prevalidation and active served-state corroboration; never expose a private key or passphrase.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Settings > SSL Settings > Upload Certificate Management path, explicit key-change statement, match-modified-settings/readability/login Criteria, no Script, DeepSeek proposal/risk and 5/0-minute estimates remain preserved; Review does not replace Upload with Generate or list-only inspection.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Perform protected local validation, one source-WebUI upload into the approved slot, required activation, verified served-chain/trust comparison and fresh WebUI access check with independent recovery available.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC firmware's Certificate Management Upload function and approved management PKI/trust path.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC/WebUI/Redfish/TLS client versions, accepted container format, crypto policy and trust bundle.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor certificate-upload/key-store/activation specification, Project PKI/TLS policy and recovery SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes input format, key binding, chain, slot, activation, trust and recovery measurable while retaining the source WebUI and login checkpoints.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Generate is a different row; local certificate validity does not prove BMC acceptance or activation; metadata listing does not prove served identity or login; API upload does not automatically prove the WebUI control.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Certificate/chain/key model and format, current state, slot/activation, trust, reconnect and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong key, chain, SAN, format or slot can break trust and management access; secret-bearing containers require protected handling; HTTP acceptance can precede a failed or pending activation.

project_override_considerations: A Project may approve a vendor API/tool for upload only if the original WebUI method, actual method, reason, engineer approval, equivalent input/key/slot/activation coverage and uncovered UI coverage are recorded. BMC-side generation or read-only certificate listing is not an equivalent override.
expected_evidence: Target/version/endpoint identity, approved format/key model/slot/activation, local certificate/key/chain validation, pre-change active chain/fingerprint/key identity and recovery approval
Source WebUI Upload screenshots and redacted audit/response evidence showing exactly one accepted write without private-key or passphrase exposure
Pending/active slot transition and activation/reconnect timeline tied to the uploaded certificate fingerprint
Actually served full-chain capture with hostname/SAN/issuer/validity/key usage/fingerprint and explicit trust result matching readable WebUI fields
Fresh WebUI/API login through the approved trust path, preserved rollback state/no retry/secret exposure and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently describe uploading certificate material, changing certificate/key state, reading back matching settings and successfully logging in. The unspecified file format and whether a private key is uploaded or an existing BMC key is bound are vendor/Project readiness inputs, not competing source purposes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The upload, state-change and post-login objective are identifiable. Vendor documentation and Project PKI inputs can define format, key binding, slot, activation and recovery, so execution readiness is pending rather than permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Keeps PACKAGE but separates Upload from Generate, rejects guessed list-only/insecure proof and adds protected key/chain validation, activation, served-trust and fresh-login evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with its critical controls and further binds the source key-change statement to either an uploaded protected key/container or documented existing BMC key, with exact source-WebUI coverage retained.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.round_02: Replaces truncated generic prose with one bounded upload state transition and independent served/access verification.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.related_source_cases: Preserves the preceding BMC-side Generate function as separate coverage; it cannot substitute for supplied-material upload.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.invalid_checkpoint_1000: No invalid draft exists for this exact source identity.

review_improvement: Prevents an insecure certificate-list response or unrelated generation from being reported as a successful upload, and protects management access and private-key secrecy through one-shot recovery-aware validation.
independent_technical_reasoning: The defining event is secure import and activation of specific owner-approved certificate material. An HTTP success, resource-list entry or locally valid certificate can coexist with a wrong key, incomplete chain, pending slot or old certificate still being served. Evidence must cryptographically identify the supplied public certificate, prove the BMC key relationship and intended active slot, then verify the live TLS endpoint and fresh WebUI login without revealing secret material.
